title: Unfair Clauses in Government Tender Specifications
what_it_is: Unfair Clauses in Government Tender Specifications

sections.label: Government procurement fairness and payment terms
sections.summary: MOF provides templates setting out parties' responsibilities, and the Standard Consultancy Agreement states agencies pay for additional services not covered by contract.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Speaker, Government agencies are required to conduct procurements in a fair manner.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: To guide agencies, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) provides templates with contractual terms and conditions which set out the responsibilities of the parties.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: For example, the Standard Consultancy Agreement (SCA), used by Government agencies for construction-related consultancy services, states that agencies will pay for additional services not covered by the contract.

sections.label: SME cash flow and design changes
sections.summary: Bulk payment at project end can cause cash flow problems for SMEs, and some tenders require unlimited design changes without additional payment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Very often, Government agencies will only make the bulk of the payment at the end of the project, creating potential cash flow problems for SMEs participating in Government tenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: And thirdly, some Government tenders require contractors to make unlimited changes to design requirements without additional payment, similar to those required by SUSS.

sections.label: SCA payment and liability limits
sections.summary: Under the SCA agencies pay for additional services, and an option to limit consultants' contractual liability becomes mandatory from 1 December 2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, on the point about making unlimited design changes, I had shared earlier that under the SCA, which is what the Government follows, the one that is used for construction-related consultancy services, agencies will pay for additional services not covered by the contract, such as further changes after design sign-off.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Then, with respect to unlimited liability, in November 2024, we added an option in the SCA to limit consultants' contractual liability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And then, as announced by Minister for National Development Mr Chee Hong Tat, last month, we will be making this mandatory starting from 1 December 2025.

sections.label: Tender Lite for SMEs
sections.summary: Tender Lite simplifies procurement in tenders up to $1 million, making it easier for businesses, especially SMEs, to access Government procurement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Besides this, the Government has introduced Tender Lite to simplify procurement in tenders with estimated procurement value up to $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This makes it easier for businesses, especially SMEs, to access Government procurement opportunities.
